speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: First, patients in public healthcare institutions enjoy subsidies of up to 80% of their bills.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Second, we have introduced MediShield Life, a universal healthcare insurance which provides all Singaporeans lifelong protection against large hospital bills and selected costly outpatient treatments, regardless of age or health condition.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Third, MediSave can be used for the balance of the bill and helps Singaporeans lower their out-of-pocket cash payments.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Taken together, this "S+3M" framework – the subsidy plus 3M – has worked well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It ensures that healthcare is affordable to Singaporeans, and no Singaporean is denied appropriate healthcare due to an inability to pay.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To underscore this point, in our public hospitals, seven in 10 subsidised bills are fully paid without any cash outlay by the patient.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In other words, 70% of all subsidised bills do not require any out-of-pocket cash payment by the patient at all.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Of the remaining 30% of bills, one-third require payment of $100 or less in cash, and another one-third of that 30% is paid for using a cash outlay of between $100 and $500.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The enhanced MediShield Life was launched in 2015.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This is a key component of our healthcare financing framework which provides universal and lifelong coverage, including for those with pre-existing illnesses.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Government provides premium subsidies to the lower- to middle-income to keep premiums affordable, and additional support to those who need more help with their premiums.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: MediShield Life aims to strike a balance between keeping premiums affordable and ensuring adequate coverage of subsidised care.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For this reason, MediShield Life has design features, such as claim limits, an annual deductible and co-insurance.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Coverage of claims and amount of payouts have improved since the introduction of the enhanced scheme.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This is up from 344,000 claims and $448 million in 2015 under the old MediShield.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The average payout per claim was $1,520 in 2017, compared to $1,300 in 2015.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For larger bills, the payout was correspondingly higher.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For the largest 10% of subsidised hospitalisation bills, which was above $4,000 in 2017, the average payout per claim was $5,800.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In comparison, MediShield paid out $4,000 on average for the largest 10% of subsidised bills in 2015.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As I had mentioned earlier, claim limits are one feature that helps MediShield Life strike a balance between keeping premiums affordable and also ensuring adequate coverage.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: MediShield Life claim limits and premiums were last revised in 2015 when the enhanced scheme was launched.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: At the time of launch, the claim limits were set to cover nine out of 10 subsidised bills.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In addition, for larger bills within claim limits, the patient’s co-payment is reduced as the claimable amount goes up, dropping from 10% to 5%, and finally to 3%.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, for illustration, for claimable amounts above $10,000, the patient’s co-payment is 3%.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For bills that exceed the claim limit, patient’s co-payment will include the remaining bill not covered by MediShield Life.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These bills tend to be for more complex cases or where patients received lower means-tested subsidies because of their higher income.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This has come down from the limits set in 2015, caused in part by increased healthcare costs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will review this and adjust the limits as necessary.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: However, even at present rates, in respect of the bills which fall outside the claim limits – in other words, outside of the eight out of 10 – about half exceed the claim limits by $230 or less.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The claim limits are necessary as they serve to keep premiums affordable.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If we are to remove the claim limits altogether, there will be significant premium increases for all Singaporeans across the board, to the order of about 30% or more.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Therefore, rather than impose this on all Singaporeans across the board, those who prefer to have higher coverage and are willing to pay higher premiums can consider private Integrated Shield Plans which can include "As-Charged" features that cover 100% of the bill.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Conversely, where patients cannot afford the cash outlay, they can tap onto MediFund as I explained earlier, or on other financial assistance schemes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In the recent case of Mr Seow Ban Yam, which Members raised, we understand that he had undergone a duct drainage procedure at the Singapore National Eye Centre (SNEC).

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The surgical procedure, which was performed by a senior consultant in an operation that took three hours, was complex, given his age.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is also not common for the procedure to be performed on both eyes at the same time.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As an indication, this was only done for seven patients out of 42,000 procedures performed by SNEC that year.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Seow's bill was about $12,000 before subsidy.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Because the SNEC bill was significantly higher than the claim limit, the payout was comparatively small, after the yearly deductible of $3,000.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: However, the balance of Mr Seow's bill was thereafter fully covered by MediSave, which meant that Mr Seow did not have to pay any cash out of pocket for the procedures which he underwent.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Nonetheless, we had asked SNEC to review their charges.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: MOH regularly reviews MediShield Life claim limits and benefits.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, we recently extended coverage to Home Parenteral Nutrition and direct admissions from emergency departments of public hospitals to community hospitals.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Last year, we also started a review of claim limits, with a view to making the appropriate adjustments as may be necessary.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This ongoing review requires a careful assessment of the appropriate claim limits and also the consequential impact it may have on premiums, to ensure that the coverage of MediShield Life remains broad-based and also sustainable.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Just as important as having a good healthcare financing framework is managing healthcare costs effectively, so that overall affordability can be maintained.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We have to work hard on this and also explore various fronts on which this can be done.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The need to monitor and manage costs and charges in public healthcare is particularly important.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The majority of Singaporeans utilise subsidised healthcare in our public healthcare institutions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We have also introduced programmes and services to help Singaporeans receive care earlier or at more appropriate settings.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, under the hospital to home programme, patients receive visits at home for a few months after hospital discharge to ensure that they recuperate well and do not get re-admitted to the hospital.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Together, these initiatives help Singaporeans manage costs and moderate increases in healthcare bills.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will keep a close watch on public healthcare costs and redouble our efforts to keep healthcare costs sustainable and affordable for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To sum up, we have a healthcare financing framework that has worked well in striving to keep healthcare affordable for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The healthcare financing framework is designed with several different but overlapping components to provide holistic support to meet Singaporeans' healthcare costs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: MediShield Life is one key component that provides Singaporeans lifelong protection against large hospital bills and selected costly outpatient treatments.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Its features are aimed at ensuring adequate coverage while keeping premiums affordable.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will continue to review, refine and strengthen MediShield Life and other components of our public healthcare financing system, and, just as importantly, manage our healthcare costs to ensure that public healthcare remains affordable for all Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: So, since SNEC is reviewing its charges, will MOH also ensure other public hospitals or other healthcare institutions offering similar procedures also review their charges to make sure that they are on par and, therefore, ensure affordability for elderly citizens?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Given the spirit of MediShield Life, such an example will not be very helpful in giving that sense of assurance in terms of healthcare affordability.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: While I am heartened that there is a review, I am wondering if the review can be brought forward, given that MediShield Life was launched quite a number of years ago.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: So, whether the review could be brought forward and, in terms of the review frequency, I understand that the Senior Minister of State is estimating around every three years.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Does this coincide with the general healthcare inflation pattern?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Yes, we have to keep healthcare cost affordable.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Members have heard me explain that that is our objective in designing the framework that we have.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And in doing so, we try to strive to do that with two broad prongs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The first, obviously, is to look at the claims limit, which is the thrust of the Member's second question.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And yes, we will review the claims limit and we will ensure that it is in tandem with the cost and ensure that the differential, as they move towards the inflationary cost for the healthcare sector, that it is kept in check and in tandem.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But, if necessary, we can always relook at the timescale as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The second prong is to deal with the charges side, because one has to look at the claim limits as one sector.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The other one is, of course, the amount of cost that is charged at the healthcare institution.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That will also be looked at to ensure that there is parity.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And that is one key aspect of trying to bring down and maintain healthcare cost to keep it affordable.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, both will be looked at at the same time.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And thereafter, we will see if that is in tandem with the trends and patterns in the healthcare industry.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: I am glad to hear that SNEC will look into the high cost of the eye duct operations.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: And how does MOH reassure Singaporeans that public healthcare costs, including the deductibles, are affordable to give them peace of mind?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If there were no deductibles, or there are no other co-payment schemes, then one would imagine that the premiums would rise and we want to ensure that, for the broader base of Singaporeans, premiums remain at a scale which is affordable.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In terms of how the deductibles are looked at, one has to consider it in the context of the kinds of treatments, the claims assessment, the actuarial assessments as well, and then when you look at that in contrast with the premiums that we want to maintain, the levels at which we want to fix the premiums, that is how the deductibles are looked at and determined.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In the context of assurance, as I have explained earlier, the healthcare financing framework is made up of not just MediShield Life.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is a combination of MediShield Life, together with MediSave and, if necessary, MediFund, along with the subsidies, all working in tandem and often overlapping with one another.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Which is why, even in the context of Mr Seow's case, which Members have heard me explain, is not quite as common as one might imagine.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Even in that situation, with the deductibles and with the co-payments after MediShield Life, the patient does not have to be out of pocket because of MediSave.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, one has to look at the entire framework working in tandem as being the framework that will sustain affordable healthcare in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Mr Seow's case, of course, has started a whole enquiry into MediShield Life and how it works amongst many members of the public.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I had a resident who has come to me, was hospitalised for two days for a minor stroke, out-of-pocket, including MediSave, from his own monies, it is about 25% of the bill.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Because that is where a large chunk of the public discussion is going to now – whether the amount of premiums collected is too high or is it just right?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: It is unclear to members of the public as to whether MediShield Life is over collecting premiums.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Some clarity on that would be helpful, in line with the spirit of the MediShield Life Review Committee report.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Well, there are two different questions at play here in Mr Pritam Singh's questions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The first obviously deals with the review of the claims limit, and that is a product of working out where the claims limit lie in the context of how many bills MediShield Life is designed to cover and looking at the healthcare cost in tandem with that and to achieve the ratio that one seeks to.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That is the review of the claims limit that I spoke about earlier.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: What Mr Singh is separately asking about is the adequacy ratio.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The adequacy ratio is something which is kept at a pace that ensures longer-term sustainability of the fund, longer-term ability to meet vicissitudes of life, and also to ensure that the MediShield Life scheme, on a longer-time basis, remains sustainable.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That is something we constantly look at as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But I want to emphasise that it is a separate issue from looking at the claims limit, which deals with the actual cost itself and how many bills are covered by MediShield Life.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The first question is in relation to claim limits for day surgeries.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: As the Senior Minister of State would know, with the advancement of technology, a number of procedures would entail patients to go through day surgeries instead of being warded in hospitals.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Could these cost-savings be taken into account in setting the claim limit for complex procedures in day surgeries?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The second question is in relation to the information flow between the national health agencies setting their costs and MOH when assessing whether or not the claim limits would be sufficient and relevant.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In the context of this case, for example, would ordinarily these healthcare agencies inform MOH, have that discussion on whether or not the price setting is appropriate before it is finalised?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There are several hundred thousand bills that are put out in our public healthcare institutions, so it is not possible to look at every bill that goes out and in discussion with the healthcare institution before that.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There are basic guidelines and benchmarks, and that is something that we look at.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, I assure the Member that we will constantly look at that and keep that within the range that fits in with the philosophy of MediShield Life.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On the question of day surgery, to some extent, shortening procedure timings or use of technology might save time and possibly expenses and money.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That would be another feature that would be looked at in the context of setting the claims limit.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As the Member knows, there are tables of charges for different procedures and these are regularly reviewed with a very broad spectrum of expertise.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Certainly, the issue as to whether or not cost savings might be gained from day surgeries or shorter surgeries or procedures which may be truncated because of technology, all these would be taken into account as we review the amount of claim limits that we have.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Senior Minister of State alluded to the adequacy ratio.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Can I ask if the Government consciously benchmarks the adequacy ratio of MediShield Life against other similar healthcare insurance schemes where the insurance is mandatory by legislation in other countries in the world?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is MediShield Life's adequacy ratio benchmarked to be similar or in the same range as the similar schemes worldwide?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second question is in relation to – if I understand the Senior Minister of State correctly – the 10% or so bills which fall above the claim limit where the difference is more than $230.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Would the Senior Minister of State be able to share with us any pertinent common characteristics in such bills?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, are they usually for older patients, where procedures may necessarily be a bit more complex?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: That may be helpful for various stakeholders out there to know what are the common characteristics as we think about this problem.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And the third question is just a clarification.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For patients whose bills go above the claim limit, are they, as matter of routine, informed by public healthcare staff that MediFund assistance that is means-tested, is available to them?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But nonetheless, there are comparables that are looked at in determining and also assessing what the adequate ratio would be.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But ultimately, we have to look at it in the context of our own domestic situation, our own claims pattern, the kind of procedures that we expect to see and also the healthcare trends that we expect in Singapore itself.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And the ratio has to be determined based on those factors.
